Suppose cppt holds data long format, prepared described Section 5.1 paper. one row per subject visit, visit = 0 visit medication dispensed, binary responses hdl_high (HDL least 60 mg/dL) ldl_low (LDL 130 mg/dL), treatment trt eight baseline covariates. analyses Tables 1 3 :
code: f <- cbind(hdl_high, ldl_low) ~ BMI + EDUC + EVDNK + EVSMK + PHYSA + PHYSB + RACE + V5AGE fit <- biscal(f, data = cppt, id = "ID", time = "visit", treatment = "trt") summary(fit)                                   # Table 1  # Table 2: smallest and largest value of each covariate (Situations 1 and 2) covs <- fit$covariate_data situations <- as.data.frame(rbind(sapply(covs, min), sapply(covs, max))) aste(fit, newdata = situations)  # Table 3: within a group defined by the discrete covariates, a Gaussian # mixture for (BMI, V5AGE), here with two components library(mixtools) grp <- with(covs, EDUC == 0 & EVDNK == 1 & EVSMK == 1 & PHYSA == 0 & PHYSB == 0 &                   RACE == 1) set.seed(1) gm <- mvnormalmixEM(as.matrix(covs[grp, c("BMI", "V5AGE")]), k = 2) rgmm <- function(M, gm) {     # draws from the fitted mixture   comp <- sample(length(gm$lambda), M, replace = TRUE, prob = gm$lambda)   out <- matrix(NA_real_, M, length(gm$mu[[1]]))   for (j in seq_along(gm$lambda)) {     idx <- which(comp == j)     z <- matrix(rnorm(length(idx) * ncol(out)), ncol = ncol(out))     out[idx, ] <- sweep(z %*% chol(gm$sigma[[j]]), 2, gm$mu[[j]], "+")   }   out } xy <- rgmm(100000, gm) draws <- data.frame(BMI = xy[, 1], EDUC = 0, EVDNK = 1, EVSMK = 1, PHYSA = 0,                     PHYSB = 0, RACE = 1, V5AGE = xy[, 2]) easte(fit, newdata = draws)
